key: Holography Principle + Kolmogorov Complexity + Mechanism Design

concepts.name: Holography Principle
concepts.short_description: Bulk information encoded on boundary; AdS/CFT correspondence, information density bounds.

concepts.name: Kolmogorov Complexity
concepts.short_description: Minimum description length of an object; algorithmic randomness, incompressibility, MDL principle.

concepts.name: Mechanism Design
concepts.short_description: Engineering rules to achieve desired outcomes with self-interested agents; auctions, incentive compatibility.

hypotheses.statement: Holographic revelation: a designer can read only an area-bounded boundary of a population of agents holding private bulk information; reconstruction of the bulk from boundary messages is possible iff K(bulk) fits the boundary capacity AND the mechanism makes strategic interior agents compress and relay.

Redundancy as incentive: holographic encoding is an erasure-correcting code; an outcome computed by decoding redundantly encoded reports could be manipulation-proof against coalitions below the code distance without payments, trading payments for redundancy.

Information rent priced in bits: the rent an agent can extract equals the conditional description length of its type given what the designer sees on the boundary, K(type|boundary); agents face a pressure between legibility (low rent, low cost) and incompressibility (high rent).

Scale tower of principals: the radial direction is a hierarchy of mechanisms, each layer aggregating and compressing reports from the layer below; the tower stops growing where compression gain per layer no longer covers the cost of keeping that layer truthful.

Fabrication is detectable by complexity: a strategic liar must fabricate data consistent with the boundary; bounded liars produce fabrications whose conditional compressibility relative to peers differs from genuine data, so the designer can audit by compression gain rather than by payments.
Occam for institutions: among mechanisms that are incentive compatible on the observed (boundary) sample of agent types, the shortest-description ones remain IC on unseen type distributions.

Minimal-cut externality: an agent's influence on the outcome is measured by the change in a minimal cut (area of the separating surface) of the communication graph, giving a geometric payment rule to set against externality (VCG) pricing.

Prequential MDL scoring rule on the boundary: agents submit a model of boundary data and are paid by the two-part code-length saving it achieves on held-out boundary segments; truthful best-available modelling should be a best response.

concept_contributions.Holography Principle: the payment is computed only on boundary data
concept_contributions.Kolmogorov Complexity: payment = bits saved under a two-part code (model cost included)
concept_contributions.Mechanism Design: the scoring rule must be incentive compatible for self-interested modellers

hypotheses.statement: Area-budgeted reconstruction: interior agents relay compressed summaries outward; the designer reads at most B*|boundary| bits; bulk reconstruction succeeds iff K(bulk) <= boundary capacity, and only when the mechanism pays relays for compression effort.

concept_contributions.Holography Principle: capacity scales with boundary, not volume
concept_contributions.Kolmogorov Complexity: the phase boundary is set by the bulk's description length
concept_contributions.Mechanism Design: relays compress only if paid; flat pay yields shirking

knockouts.Holography Principle: capacity scales with volume; no transition at K = capacity

hypotheses.statement: Code-decoded outcome rule: each agent's report is a symbol of a codeword with distance d; the outcome is the decoded message; coalitions smaller than d/2 cannot shift the outcome, so manipulation resistance comes from redundancy instead of payments.

concept_contributions.Holography Principle: redundant boundary encoding with a recovery threshold
concept_contributions.Kolmogorov Complexity: nothing essential: distance, not description length, is the invariant
concept_contributions.Mechanism Design: coalition manipulation is the threat model

knockouts.Holography Principle: no redundancy: any single liar shifts the outcome

questions.what_can_transfer: code family to other outcome rules
questions.distinguishing_observable: manipulation-rate step at k ~ d/2 versus a matched-redundancy random-parity null

hypotheses.statement: Complexity rent: the designer pays each agent a rent proportional to an estimate of K(type|boundary); over repeated play, agents are selected to present types that are legible or incompressible depending on the rent's sign.

concept_contributions.Holography Principle: conditioning variable is the boundary the designer sees
concept_contributions.Kolmogorov Complexity: rent measured in conditional description length
concept_contributions.Mechanism Design: rent is an information rent of a mechanism

knockouts.Holography Principle: conditioning on nothing; rent becomes unconditional complexity

hypotheses.statement: Holographic organism: an agent's internal state is readable only via an interface tape whose capacity scales with its surface; to be paid by a truthful-report mechanism the organism must compress its internal policy onto that surface.

hypotheses.statement: Revelation principle under a description cap: when messages must be shorter than K(type), direct truthful mechanisms fail and multi-round indirect mechanisms become necessary; the welfare gap is a function of K(type) minus message budget.

concept_contributions.Kolmogorov Complexity: type complexity sets the required budget

hypotheses.statement: Occam for institutions: a designer searching mechanism programs prefers the shortest that are IC on observed type samples; shorter IC mechanisms should remain IC under distribution shift.

hypotheses.statement: Wedge-decodability dictionary: represent a strategic population by its boundary transcript and ask which interior agents' types are decodable from each boundary subregion; test nesting and complementary recovery.

lenses.name: Wedge-decodability map
lenses.rationale: Holography predicts nested, complementary reconstruction; test whether strategic transcripts reproduce this structure.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: boundary transcripts of a grid of agents under a mechanism
lenses.transformation: for each contiguous boundary subregion A, decode each interior agent's type from A's transcript with a fixed decoder; record the decodable set W(A)
observables: nesting violations: A subset of B but W(A) not subset of W(B)
complementary recovery: W(A) union W(complement of A) covers interior
predictedSignals: threshold in |W(A)| near |A| = half the boundary
zero nesting violations under the IC mechanism
lenses.nullExpectation: decodability grows linearly with |A| with no threshold; violation rate equals a random-routing null
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: geometric (nested) structure of reconstruction, not a single accuracy number

lenses.name: Rent-per-bit ledger
lenses.rationale: Tests whether information rents track conditional description length.
lenses.transformation: estimate K(type|boundary) by compressed-length difference with two estimators (lzma and an order-k context coder); regress rent on it
observables: slope of rent vs conditional K estimate
predictedSignals: positive slope stable across both estimators
lenses.nullExpectation: rent correlates only with raw type length
failureModes: both estimators share a blind spot

lenses.name: Capacity-transition locator
lenses.rationale: Description length against boundary capacity is the core holography-Kolmogorov claim; locate where reconstruction fails.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: reconstruction error across grid size L, per-link budget B, generator program length l
lenses.transformation: for each (L,B,l) compute exact-reconstruction rate; fit transition point in ratio r = l/(4L*B)
predictedSignals: under flat pay failure whenever L^2 > 4L*B
lenses.nullExpectation: no dependence on l when generator structure is hidden from relays
failureModes: search cap, not K, sets the transition
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates capacity-bound failure from incentive failure

lenses.name: Coalition erasure spectrum
lenses.rationale: Treat collusion as corruption of codeword symbols.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: outcome rule, coalition size k, coalition best response
lenses.transformation: for each k sample coalitions and compute best manipulation by exhaustive search over coalition reports; record success rate
predictedSignals: step at k ~ d/2 for the code rule
lenses.nullExpectation: smooth rise from k=1 for a random-parity rule with matched redundancy
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: collusion robustness expressed as a code parameter

lenses.name: Fabrication compression-gain audit
lenses.rationale: Distinguish genuine from fabricated reports by conditional compressibility.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: reports of honest and lying agents with peer reports
lenses.transformation: score = C(peers+report) - C(peers) (conditional compressed length); rank reporters
lenses.nullExpectation: AUC ~ 0.5 once marginal statistics are matched

lenses.name: Mechanism-length generalization curve
lenses.sourceRepresentation: enumerated mechanism programs in a tiny grammar
lenses.transformation: compute train IC regret, keep zero-regret programs, compute OOD regret, correlate with program length
predictedSignals: rho >= 0.3 between length and OOD regret
lenses.nullExpectation: rho ~ 0, or explained by count of numeric constants
failureModes: grammar biases short programs toward canonical auctions
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: links description length to robustness of incentives

lenses.name: Radial compression profile
lenses.rationale: Checks for an emergent scale direction in relay networks.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: relay network and per-node message sizes
lenses.transformation: bin nodes by depth; compute mean compression ratio per depth
predictedSignals: ratio increases with depth; depth ~ log n
lenses.nullExpectation: shortest-path tree shows the same profile
failureModes: profile fixed by grid geometry alone

experiments.hypothesis: An outcome rule that decodes agents' reports as a codeword of distance d resists manipulation by any coalition of size k < d/2 without payments, while a rule with matched redundancy but no distance does not.
experiments.mechanism: n=31 agents each hold one symbol of a BCH(31,16,d=7) codeword encoding the true 16-bit public decision; reports are symbols; outcome = nearest-codeword decode. Coalition members prefer a different outcome and choose reports jointly.
experiments.intervention: coalition sizes k = 1..8; coalition searches its members' reports exhaustively (2^k options) for any report vector changing the decoded outcome
experiments.control: random-parity rule: same 31 report bits, outcome = 16 fixed random XOR parities of the reports (no minimum distance), same redundancy ratio
experiments.positive_control: direct rule: outcome bits read from 16 agents (d=1); k=1 must manipulate in >= 0.99 of coalitions
experiments.observable: manipulation success rate: fraction of sampled coalitions that can change the decoded outcome, per k
experiments.success_criterion: code rule: success rate <= 0.02 for all k <= 3 AND >= 0.5 for k >= 4, over 20 seeds x 200 coalitions; random-parity null: success rate >= 0.5 at k = 1
experiments.failure_criterion: code rule success rate > 0.02 at any k <= 3; or null success rate < 0.5 at k = 1 (world broken)
experiments.alternative_explanation: the standard minimum-distance decoding bound; coding theory with agents renamed
experiments.null_twin: random-parity rule with matched report count, per-report entropy and outcome entropy, but no minimum distance
experiments.why_this_implementation: explicit linear codes over GF(2) are the smallest faithful discrete analog of holographic erasure correction; no ML needed
experiments.size: 31 agents, 16-bit message, k=1..8, 200 coalitions per k, 20 seeds, exhaustive 2^k search
stupid_explanations: the threshold is exactly the textbook decoding radius, so nothing new
restricting coalition search to own symbols guarantees the result
majority/repetition voting would show the same robustness

experiments.hypothesis: With per-bit relay costs, bulk reconstruction from an area-bounded boundary succeeds iff the bulk's description length fits boundary capacity, but only when relays are paid for compression; under flat pay relays shirk and failure sets in whenever raw volume exceeds capacity.
experiments.mechanism: L x L grid of agents; bulk bits generated by a random program of length l in a 16-opcode stack VM (so K <= l + c); interior agents relay outward; each relay chooses an encoding from {raw-truncate, lzma, VM-program search up to l_max} with effort cost; designer reads 4L*B bits and reconstructs; payment is MDL (paid bits saved on audited cells) or flat
experiments.intervention: vary l in 8 log-spaced values 8..256, L in {8,12,16}, B in {1,2,4}; switch payment MDL vs flat; relays reach a fixed point by iterated best response
experiments.control: flat payment with identical costs and budgets
experiments.positive_control: l = 8 with MDL pay must reconstruct exactly at all L
experiments.observable: exact-reconstruction rate; fitted transition ratio r* = l/(4L*B) at 50% exact reconstruction
experiments.success_criterion: under MDL pay r* in [0.5, 2] for every (L,B); under flat pay exact-reconstruction rate <= 0.1 whenever L^2 > 4L*B; 10 seeds per cell
experiments.failure_criterion: MDL-pay r* outside [0.5, 2] for any (L,B); or MDL vs flat exact-reconstruction difference < 0.2 at matched cells
experiments.alternative_explanation: source coding theorem plus the fact that paying for effort buys effort
experiments.null_twin: same VM output XORed with a fixed secret pseudorandom mask unknown to relays: matched marginal bit statistics and same true K up to the mask seed, but generator structure unavailable to relays
experiments.why_this_implementation: a tiny VM gives an upper bound on K by construction instead of relying only on a compressor estimate
experiments.size: L in {8,12,16}, B in {1,2,4}, 8 values of l, 10 seeds, program search capped at 1e5 candidates
stupid_explanations: the transition reflects the program-search cap, not K
paying for effort trivially yields effort
flat-pay failure is baked in by the cost choice

experiments.hypothesis: Bounded-program liars trying to shift an aggregate outcome produce reports whose conditional compressed length given honest peers is anomalous, detectable even after matching unigram and bigram statistics.
experiments.mechanism: 40 reporters observe segments of a structured source (order-3 Markov with a planted repeated motif); 8 liars emit 512-symbol reports from generators of <= 64 VM instructions chosen to push the mean statistic upward; audit score = C(peers+report) - C(peers) with lzma and a context coder
experiments.intervention: liars optimize their generator by hill-climbing to maximize outcome shift subject to matching unigram and bigram frequencies within 1%
experiments.control: liars sampling from the true source (no lie): AUC must be within 0.5 +/- 0.05
experiments.positive_control: naive liars emitting biased i.i.d. bits: AUC must be >= 0.95
experiments.observable: ROC AUC of audit score, liar vs honest
experiments.success_criterion: mean AUC >= 0.75 for matched-statistics liars across 20 seeds, with 95% bootstrap CI lower bound > 0.6
experiments.alternative_explanation: liars miss a third-order statistic that any n-gram test would catch
experiments.null_twin: liars that match unigram, bigram and trigram statistics by resampling from the source's own trigram table with a bias, removing any program-length signature
experiments.why_this_implementation: liars as short programs make 'bounded fabrication' literal; a neural generator was displaced because its capacity is not measured in description length
experiments.size: 40 reporters, 8 liars, 512 symbols each, 20 seeds, 2000 hill-climb steps
stupid_explanations: detection comes from an unmatched higher-order n-gram

experiments.hypothesis: Among single-item auction programs that are incentive compatible on a training value distribution, shorter programs have lower IC regret under distribution shift.
experiments.mechanism: grammar of allocation/payment rules over sorted bids (max, second, reserve constants, arithmetic, conditionals); enumerate all programs up to 9 tokens; evaluate max gain from unilateral deviation for 3 bidders
experiments.intervention: train on uniform[0,1] values; test on beta(0.5,0.5), exponential(1) clipped, and correlated values
experiments.control: random selection among train-IC mechanisms regardless of length
experiments.positive_control: second-price auction must have zero OOD regret
experiments.observable: Spearman rho between program length and mean OOD regret among train-IC programs
experiments.success_criterion: rho >= 0.3 with permutation p < 0.01, AND rho >= 0.2 after partialling out number of numeric constants
experiments.failure_criterion: rho < 0.1, or partial rho < 0.1 after controlling for constant count
experiments.alternative_explanation: longer programs carry more reserve constants tuned to the training distribution; ordinary overfitting
experiments.null_twin: length labels permuted within train-regret strata, preserving the regret distribution
experiments.why_this_implementation: an enumerable grammar gives exact description length; no learned mechanism network needed
experiments.size: programs up to 9 tokens (~1e5), 3 bidders, 2000 value profiles per distribution, 20-point deviation grid
stupid_explanations: only canonical auctions survive the train filter, so rho measures grammar bias
deviation grid too coarse to see small violations
